correctness.rationale: All-size exact proof: weighted arrowhead Laplacian products produce hub-edge cubic and leaf-leaf quadratic identities; positive discriminant margins show leaf-leaf entries and diagonals remain strictly positive; 9AC−4B²>0 follows from v≤b² and yields strict cubic monotonicity; the positive quadratic comparison orders all hub edges by conductance. Stochasticity plus Perron–Frobenius proves the strict Euclidean stability gap for unequal weights; uniform star eigenvalues give equality. Independently replayed 42,875 exact-rational rational-matrix checks are supplementary, not universal evidence.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The strongest potentially dominating statement is the explicit fourth-order RK4 formula on all UNWEIGHTED bipartite graphs: it guarantees a unique edge-first failure and can be specialized to uniform stars, but its domain excludes freely varying spoke conductances. The broader Taylor theorem similarly assumes unweighted complete multipartite graphs. The arbitrary-weight Gauss theorem has the same object but a different rational map, not interchangeable with R4. In contrast, the new theorem shows a single maximum-weight edge bottleneck for any number of unequal spokes and proves strict loss before the spectral boundary, using a positive quadratic comparison and irreducible Perron argument. These additions are not direct stated implications of the compared claims; publication priority remains conditional on inaccessible sources.

value.rationale: Exact all-size positivity and spectral-stability threshold for a physically motivated heterogeneous diffusion hub network, with no floating-point tuning, unique one-dimensional cubic and structural largest-conductance failure law. Demonstrates a robust positivity/stability separation absent in uniform networks; applicable to timestep selection under arbitrarily varying link strengths. Not a mere isolated scalar computation or a known uniform-star table.
